story_type: helicopter bucket drop on a prairie fire, door camera
hook: A Black Hawk crew dropped a bucket of water right on the flames.
narration: A Black Hawk crew dropped a full bucket of water right on the flames.
This was October twelfth, twenty twenty-four, north of Bismarck, North Dakota.
Long lines of fire were eating across the dry prairie.
The bucket hangs on a cable under the helicopter, so the crew can scoop it full from a lake without ever landing.
Then they fly back and open it right over the edge where the fire is spreading.
From the air, the burn stretched about five miles long.
[short pause] Roughly twenty-two hundred acres went black.
outcome: By the next day, the fire was one hundred percent contained.
title: Black Hawk bucket drop on a wildfire
description:
North Dakota Army National Guard aircrews fought wildland fires north of Bismarck, North Dakota, on Oct. 12, 2024, filmed from the helicopter's door. Burleigh County reported the fire 100% contained on Oct. 13 after about 2,200 to 2,300 acres burned.

Footage: U.S. Army National Guard video by Staff Sgt. Leif Anderson, North Dakota National Guard, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/940075/north-dakota-national-guard-responds-wildfire
